topic: how a tire company created the Michelin Guide to get people driving more
storyAngle: A tire maker wanted more driving, so it printed a guidebook, and the guidebook became the thing restaurants are judged by.
doNotClaim: Do not say how stars are awarded or who the inspectors are.
Do not give any restaurant, chef or city.
The 1900 aim is as stated in the guide itself: to help motorists, which would raise demand for cars and so for tires.

facts.claim: The first Michelin Guide appeared in 1900, published by the tire-making Michelin brothers for French motorists, with information on fuel, repairs, lodging and food.
The brothers published it to increase demand for cars and therefore for tires: tires wear out through use, so more driving means more tire sales.
Nearly 35,000 copies of the first edition were printed and given free to motorists.
In 1926 the guide began awarding stars to restaurants, at first only a single star.
Michelin stars are today one of the most closely watched restaurant ratings in the world.
